title: Health Plan Cost Calculator
purpose: Students discover that the cheapest-premium plan is not always the cheapest plan overall by calculating total annual costs under different usage scenarios.
learning_objectives: Calculate total annual health insurance costs (premiums + out-of-pocket)
Apply deductible, coinsurance, and out-of-pocket maximum concepts to real scenarios
Match plan choice to anticipated health status and medical needs

scenarios.name: Healthy Year
scenarios.description: One annual physical (preventive, covered at 100%) + one urgent care visit with X-ray
scenarios.details: Annual physical: $0 out-of-pocket (preventive care). Urgent care: $350 total bill.

scenarios.name: Moderate Year
scenarios.description: Four primary care visits, one specialist visit, one MRI, monthly prescriptions
scenarios.details: 4 doctor visits ($150 each = $600), 1 specialist ($250), 1 MRI ($3,500), 12 months prescriptions ($40/month = $480). Total: $4,830.

scenarios.name: High-Need Year
scenarios.description: Emergency appendectomy with 2-day hospital stay + follow-up care
scenarios.details: Appendectomy and hospital stay ($22,000), follow-up care and medications ($1,500). Total: $23,500.

calculation_steps: Determine out-of-pocket costs: medical bills until deductible met (pay 100%)
Apply coinsurance to bills after deductible (pay your percentage)
Cap total out-of-pocket at the OOP maximum
Add premiums + out-of-pocket for total annual cost

reflection_questions.question: Which plan had the cheapest premium? Did it win in any scenarios?
reflection_questions.expected_insight: Plan C (Bronze HDHP) has the cheapest premium and wins in the healthy scenario, but loses in moderate and high-need scenarios.

reflection_questions.question: Under what circumstances would you choose Plan C over Plan A?
reflection_questions.expected_insight: Choose Plan C if you're young, healthy, rarely see doctors, and want to save on premiums while building HSA savings.

reflection_questions.question: Write a 2-sentence summary comparing plans
reflection_questions.prompt: Plan C is the cheapest if... but Plan A is the cheapest if...
reflection_questions.sample_answer: Plan C is the cheapest if you stay healthy and have minimal medical expenses because the low premium saves money. Plan A is the cheapest if you have a major medical event because the low out-of-pocket maximum caps your costs.

teacher_notes: Common student errors: forgetting to add premiums, not capping at OOP max, copay confusion. Circulate and ask 'What did this person pay every month even before they got sick?' to catch the premium-omission error.
